title: The Suite keeps Proofs, and a check names what it ignores

statements.says: The Suite keeps a Proof each time a check passes: the check, and the exact inputs it passed on.
A check whose inputs match a Proof does not run.
A check's inputs are every file in the worktree that git does not ignore, less the paths the check lists under ignores.
The Suite reads the tree as it is, and no longer reads a diff or a base commit.
ignores replaces when.
A Suite file that still has when is turned down, with a message that says how to rewrite it.
A Suite in which every check has a Proof passes.
The Suite's output names each Proof beside what ran.
Proofs belong to one clone and never leave it.
Every worktree and every loop in the clone shares the Proofs.
A Proof has no age limit.
After each loop run that landed a ticket, a full run on the newest main trusts no Proof and uses no image.
A check that goes red in the full run loses its Proofs, and the loop stops and reports.
A check may name an image, a Dockerfile in the repo's Steering, and the Suite builds it and runs the check inside it on a copy of exactly the files its Proof reads.
This repo's Suite file sets runs to 1.
An agent may run the Suite with skillworks-suite, and the Proofs it writes count for the driver.
The Suite took about 46% of each ticket, and across 56 landed tickets it ran for a median of 17 minutes.
The Suite ran again at landing whenever main had moved.
Most checks had no when, so they ran on every ticket.
A change that woke no check ran every check, so a docs-only ticket paid the full Suite.
Running an image check on a copy of exactly the files its Proof reads makes what was proved and what was tested the same set.
A path left off an ignores list only runs a check that did not need to run, while a path left off a when list lets a check sleep and a red change lands.
Across 56 landed tickets, a second run never turned a red Suite green.
With Proofs, a red circuit, a landing after a rebase and a lost push race run only the checks whose inputs are new, and most landings run nothing.
Because the Proofs an agent writes count for the driver, an agent that checks its own work does not cost the ticket twice.

Exact when lists held by tests, keeping the diff and rerunning at landing only checks both sides woke, were rejected: they are easier to explain, but a path left off a when list lets a red change land.
Exact when lists were also rejected because a when list needs a line for every file a test reads, and six such hidden reads were found at once.

Making a Proof expire after 24 hours, to catch a change outside the repo such as a new SDK, was rejected, because that change is rare, the full run after each loop run catches it, and a clock only adds runs that prove nothing new.
Sharing Proofs through the remote as git notes, so a teammate's pass would count, was rejected, because a Proof holds on the machine that made it and a pass on one OS proves nothing on another.
Keeping the rule that a Suite that ran nothing cannot pass was turned down, because a Proof is a real pass on the same inputs, so the guard has nothing left to guard.

This replaces the when half of the earlier decision that the Suite runs its checks together, and the rule that a change that wakes no check runs every check, while running the checks together still holds.
Setting runs to 1 replaces an earlier decision that asked for 2 because the container tests flaked.
A later note says this repo's Suite file now sets runs to 2, so that a check that goes red and then passes shows as a Flake, and the rest of the decision stands.
